items.title: Where German is spoken
items.claim: German is an official or co-official language of how many European countries?

options.text: Six (Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Belgium)

items.reveal_title: Six European states give German official status
items.reveal:
It is the sole official language in Liechtenstein and one of multiple in Belgium (East Cantons), Luxembourg, Switzerland and Italy's South Tyrol.

German is the most widely spoken native language in the EU (around 95 million).
items.why: Language geography rarely matches state borders neatly.

items.title: When the Duden first appeared
items.claim: Konrad Duden's first orthographic dictionary was published in which year?
items.reveal:
Duden's Vollstandiges Orthographisches Worterbuch der deutschen Sprache appeared in Leipzig in 1880.

A standard Orthographische Konferenz in 1901 made it the de facto national reference, a role it has held since.
items.why: Standardisation of writing systems was a late 19th-century project across Europe.

items.title: Brecht's Verfremdungseffekt
items.claim: Bertolt Brecht's theatre theory is widely translated as 'alienation effect'. What does Verfremdungseffekt specifically aim to do?

options.text: Make audiences identify completely with characters
Disrupt emotional immersion so the audience thinks critically about the social conditions depicted
Make plays as short as possible

items.reveal:
Brecht developed the concept from the late 1920s. Verfremdung is closer to 'making strange' than to ordinary alienation.

The Berliner Ensemble, founded with Helene Weigel in 1949, became its main institutional home.
items.why: Translation choices can shift the apparent meaning of a theoretical term.
